C0.quote: When multiple voters provide preference orders or rankings on candidates
C0.note: Kemeny-style aggregation of voters' rankings with a fairness constraint. It is borderline with ML/IR rank aggregation (applications include web search; datasets are expert and movie rankings), but it is framed as aggregating voters' rankings into a consensus, so coded ELIG.

C1.quote: we first provide a novel algorithm that achieves (2 + ε)-approximation
C1.note: EM: experiments on real-world ranking datasets (football experts, Movielens).

C2.1.value: input rankings; preference orders or rankings; set S of rankings
C2.1.quote: Given a set S of rankings over d candidates

C2.2.quote: We refer to the set of all rankings (or permutations) over [d]

C2.3.quote: it is essentially influenced by the preference order of a single voter
C2.3.note: Only the term 'preference order' is used. It is not defined separately from the submitted rankings.

C2.4.quote: voters provide preference orders or rankings on candidates
C2.4.note: IDU and ONE fit about equally well (the input is described both as provided rankings and as preference orders), so the first-listed code was chosen.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare or satisfaction notions are used for voters.

C5.1.quote: contain at least ⌊αi · k⌋ candidates from Gi
C5.1.note: Fairness concerns the representation of candidate groups, not voters. The objective is the sum of Kendall tau distances.

C6.VOT.reason: The codebook counts fixed actions as actions, and voters providing rankings that the rule aggregates is such a fixed action, so voters are present and NONSTRAT (implicit).
